summary: Lifecycle-recovery-only phase (no engineering functionality changed; no contract or architecture revision; runtime unchanged, Observed/observe/unavailable). Investigated why the operator did not receive Phase 145H.3's canonical report notification. Direct repository inspection found the git-tracked canonical report (docs/PHASE_145H3_*.md) present, complete, and pushed -- never the source of the symptom. The local, gitignored canonical report pair (.pcae/phase-reports/latest.json/latest.md) was found inconsistent: latest.json had been hand-patched to identify 145H.3 but latest.md still held 145H.2's content, and no timestamped archival pair existed. Root cause, reconstructed from provenance history and direct source inspection: both pcae phase complete attempts for 145H.3 (19:27:36 and 19:28:09 UTC) were correctly rejected by the Repository Transition Validator's cross-phase commit contamination check, because .pcae/phase-completion-metadata.json still identified the prior phase (145H.2) at the moment each attempt ran -- hand-corrected only afterward. This is the same defect lineage documented and self-corrected at Phase 145G.3 (docs/PHASE_145G3R_...md), 145H.1, and 145H.2, now recurring a fourth time; complete_phase() unconditionally releases the agent lock before the validator ever runs, so each rejection also cost a lock-release/reacquire cycle. Because rejection happened upstream of finalize_phase_report()'s write step, neither attempt wrote any report artifact or reached notification-intent creation -- classified NOTIFICATION_DISPATCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED, not a dispatch failure or suppressed retry. Confirmed via .pcae/phase-reports/.last-notified.json that no 145H.3 delivery of any kind existed prior to this phase, making a retry safe under the exactly-once rule. With metadata already self-consistent (from the prior session's hand-authoring) and explicit human authorization obtained before firing a real outbound Telegram message, retried pcae phase complete: the transition validator accepted, the local canonical report pair was regenerated consistently (both latest.* and a new timestamped archival pair), and exactly one Telegram notification was sent and confirmed via a real [telegram]: OK provider response -- not an assumed marker. Verdict: RECOVERED -- CANONICAL REPORT AND TERMINAL NOTIFICATION CONSISTENT.
